subject: Orchestration channel retries in private deployment — initial report and timeline
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom@acme-health.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-27T22:15:00Z
Subject: Observed orchestration-channel retries in our private deployment

Jordan —

We started seeing a spike in inference errors and 500s from our private cluster around 21:50 UTC. Our engineers traced it to repeated orchestration-channel retries between the customer-side agent and Redwood's control channel. The symptom: short-lived request failures (0.5–2s) that then succeed after a retry, but overall SLA impact is visible in our synthetic checks.

Key facts from our side: 
- First spike: ~21:48 UTC, widespread across two availability zones.
- Errors: transient 500s and client-level timeouts; most resolve on a second attempt.
- We pulled kvcache logs and see numerous handshakes failing with timeout 100ms -> retry.

Can your team confirm whether there was a coordination/upgrade event on Redwood's side? We are concerned about any in-flight orchestration rollout that could have affected the control channel.

Attaching a short snippet of the logs we collected. Please advise next steps — we need an ETA for a mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Health
(attachment: kvcache-logs-20270527.txt)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <tom@acme-health.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-28T00:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed orchestration-channel retries in our private deployment

Tom —

Thanks for the quick heads up and the log excerpt. We're pulling telemetry now. At a glance this looks like a retry amplification in the orchestration control channel coinciding with a rolling configuration push in one of the agent pools.

Immediate actions: 
- I have asked the on-call infra team to pause the rollout and snapshot agent configs (Ben).
- We'll enable extended handshakes and increase control-channel timeout on the affected pools to reduce retry bounces.
- We'll provide a customer-facing remediation timeline within 2 hours.

We're treating this as a severity-2 and will share a running update. Sorry for the disruption — we'll get you an ETA ASAP.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <tom@acme-health.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-28T03:10:00Z
Subject: Update: remediation steps and temporary mitigation applied

Tom / Acme Ops —

Quick update from the Redwood side after the initial investigation: 

What happened (short): 
- During a routine rolling configuration push to private-agent pools, a subset of agents briefly entered a higher backoff state when the orchestration channel handshake timeout was not extended for longer RTTs observed in two AZs. That caused clustered retries which raised error surface for short windows.

Mitigation we've applied (now live): 
- Paused the rolling push and rolled back the config on the two affected agent pools.
- Increased orchestration-channel handshake timeout from 100ms -> 300ms for those pools.
- Enabled additional telemetry and a circuit-breaker to prevent retry amplification on future pushes.

Customer impact: 
- Intermittent request failures between 21:48–22:10 UTC on 2027-05-27; most requests retried successfully within 1–2 seconds. 
- No data loss; inference outputs that previously errored were re-evaluated on retry.

Next steps & timeline: 
- We will run a controlled canary tomorrow (2027-05-29 02:00 UTC) with tighter telemetry gates.
- Post-incident package (timeline, root cause evidence, logs) will be shared by 2027-06-02.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a bridge during the canary window to watch telemetry together.

Attachments included: remediation_timeline-20270528.pdf (summary), kvcache-logs-20270527.txt (excerpt).

If you have any immediate constraints (e.g., no-canary windows), tell us and we'll adapt.

Thanks for flagging this — full post-incident info coming.

— Jordan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: remediation_timeline-20270528.pdf)

From: Tom Ellis <tom@acme-health.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-28T05:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Update: remediation steps and temporary mitigation applied

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick remediation and the short write-up. A couple quick asks from our side: 

1) Can you confirm whether the rollback preserved rolling-order affinity (we had a few long-lived streams that might have been affected)?
2) Please include the exact PR/config hash that was rolled back so our change control can reconcile.

We are okay with the canary tomorrow but would like to join the bridge for the first 30 minutes. Please schedule a 30-min slot starting 02:00 UTC and send the invite.

Thanks — Tom
Ops, Acme Health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Tom Ellis <tom@acme-health.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-02T14:30:00Z
Subject: Post-incident package: findings, evidence, and follow-up actions

Tom / Acme team —

Attached is the post-incident package for the orchestration-channel retry incident: 
- Root cause: configuration push with insufficient handshake timeout for high-latency AZs; retry amplification when combined with short client timeouts.
- Evidence: captured agent logs (excerpt attached), control-channel telemetry graphs, and the rollback PR hash: commit a9c3f7b.
- Actions taken: rollback, timeout increase, circuit-breaker addition, and a follow-up patch to the rollout controller to gate on cross-AZ RTT variance.
- Preventive items: automated rollout gates for control-channel latencies, expanded canary coverage for private deployments, and runbook updates.

We validated the canary on 2027-05-29 and observed no recurrence in the affected pools. The attached remediation_timeline-20270528.pdf summarizes milestones; kvcache-logs-20270527.txt contains the log excerpts we referenced.

Next steps we recommend for Acme: 
- Confirm whether you want automatic rollback enforcement for your private pools (we can enable this per-account).
- Optional 1:1 review of the incident with our engineering team (we can include the agent owners and rollout engineers).

If useful, we'd like to schedule a follow-up review the week of 2027-06-07 to walk through the technical details and any action items for your change control team.

Thanks for partnering closely during this — apologies again for the disruption.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
(attachments: remediation_timeline-20270528.pdf, kvcache-logs-20270527.txt)
